intro: In Demre, in Antalya province, stands the Church of St Nicholas, a monastery and church of the 6th century AD. Nicholas of Myra — the source of the Father Christmas story — was buried here, and the church still keeps its floor mosaics and part of its frescoes in place.
history: The church rose over the tomb of Nicholas, bishop of Myra in the fourth century, and under Byzantium it became a major place of pilgrimage. Then, in 1087, Italian merchants carried most of the saint's bones off to Bari. The building you see today stands on the site of a 6th-century church; it was largely rebuilt in the eighth century and has been repaired several times since.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the sarcophagus of St Nicholas, the floor mosaics and the frescoes, and look for the synthronon too.
facts: Did you know? The story of Nicholas secretly leaving dowries for poor girls grew, over the centuries, into the figure of Father Christmas. The church was built over the tomb of Nicholas, bishop of Myra, and became a major place of pilgrimage. And in 1087 Italian merchants carried most of the saint's bones off to Bari.
outro: This brings our journey through the Church of St Nicholas to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
